chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Learning music in the public schools; defending America
summary: He credits public schools with his music training and a white supervisor with putting him in the orchestra, and says there are ways to work out racial conflict.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: You had learned that in school.

I had studied typing, yes. As I told you I studied everything that was given in the schools and I told you yesterday -- you asked me where had I learned my music, who was my supervisor. Well, in the public schools in America, which is one of the great things about America -- I want to get back to saying that because I think this is very important. Because even though I've been -- my father was a fighter for integration, and I have lived a life of integration all my life. Not by force, as I said, but by invitation.

And regardless of that, as I said, the United States of America, from my estimation from my travels, has got to be if not the greatest country in the world one of the greatest countries in the world, of all times. And I say that to say that to say this, that the music that I did learn, even though I was of a black race, and was underprivileged, I did have through the public schools an opportunity to learn music, through the public school system. And I always stress this when I'm talking to anybody about an interview, because I want that to be known and I want it to be understood that there is a way, and it has been shown in America that there is a way to work out racial conflict. And there has been improvements made.

It's unfortunate that some of it has come about by violence, but it is through the public schools that I learned how to play music, learned how to play the violin, went into the citywide orchestra because I was chosen by white supervisor who was teaching music and didn't show any bias. So I don't want to be recorded as one of those people who are so narrowminded as to feel that there is nothing right with America.
Because I'm one of those people who thinks everything is right with America except no one is perfect, as America is not perfect. No country is perfect, no people are perfect.
But I am very appreciative of this fact, that I did learn music in public schools. It was worth -- I may not have been able to afford the private lessons.
